He was a member of the high school's top-ranked [[Mater Dei Basketball|Mater Dei Monarchs basketball team]]. Bozeman later played [[college basketball]] with the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]]. During his freshman year, he played in 26 games (21 starts) and was an Honorable-Mention Pac-10 All-Freshman Team Selection after averaging 3.5 assists per game (8th In Pac-10). At the UCLA Basketball Banquet Awards he won the Seymour Armond Memorial Award as the most valuable freshman. As a junior, he started all 28 games, and led the Pac-10 in assists per game (5.5) and assists (155). At the end of the year banquet, he was given the Bruin Hoopsters JD Morgan memorial award for outstanding team play. ==Professional career== Bozeman was [[Undrafted|not drafted]] in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]], but found his way into the league through the [[Atlanta Hawks]] where he averaged 1.1 points in 23 games with five starts before being waived in January 2007.[http://www.courant.com/sports/hc-nbaup0104.artjan04,0,3492875.story?coll=hc-headlines-sports Hawks waive Bozeman]{{Dead link|date=April 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} Soon thereafter he was quickly picked up by the [[Albuquerque Thunderbirds]] of the NBA D-League.[http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=3417549 Thunderbirds Defeat D-Fenders in First Ever Meeting] Bozeman went overseas to play for the [[Belgium]]-based [[Base Oostende|Telindus Oostende]] basketball club and averaged 4.6 points per game over ten games.[https://web.archive.org/web/20231108183937/https://www.scouting4u.com/player.asp?id=1963 Scouting4u.com] The former Bruin went on to play another season in [[Europe]], this time with the [[Poland|Polish]] [[Czarni Słupsk]] club during the 2007–08 season.[http://www.eurobasket.com/team.asp?Cntry=POL&Team=153&Year=2007-2008 ENERGA CZARNI SLUPSK basketball team] In 2010, he signed with Belgacom Liège in Belgium.{{Cite web |url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/belgium/12133/belgacom_liege_adds_taylor_griffin_and_cedric_bozeman.html |title=Belgacom Liege adds Taylor Griffin and Cedric Bozeman |access-date=2010-08-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100908133933/http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/belgium/12133/belgacom_liege_adds_taylor_griffin_and_cedric_bozeman.html |archive-date=2010-09-08 |url-status=dead }} For the 2011–12 season, Bozeman joined the [[Reno Bighorns]] of the [[NBDL]]. At the end of December 2011, the Bighorns waived Bozeman due to injury.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/reno/bighorns_acquire_adrian_oliver_2011_12_30.html |title=NBA Development League: Bighorns Acquire Adrian Oliver |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2012-01-16 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130812003138/http://www.nba.com/dleague/reno/bighorns_acquire_adrian_oliver_2011_12_30.html |archive-date=2013-08-12 }} However, he later rejoined the team. In 2012, he joined the [[Barangay Ginebra Kings]] of [[Philippine Basketball Association]] as their import for the Governors Cup. Later in 2012, he signed with the [[Westports Malaysia Dragons]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.aseanbasketballleague.com/news/detail/7103/westports-malaysia-dragons-sign-cedric-bozeman-and-gavin-edwards
